messages:
sara: quick heads-up — I’m seeing a perf regression on FP8 decode for long-context requests (~8k). TTFT is ~2.3x higher when microbatching is enabled. digging in now. :grimacing:

dmitri: can you paste the profiler output / logs? did this start after the kernel-selector tweak yesterday?

sara: looks aligned with that change. snippet from runtime trace: ```text
[2026-04-02T13:01:05Z] kernel-router: selected kernel fp8_hybrid_packed_gemm for decode
[2026-04-02T13:01:05Z] kv-cache: allocate 65MB pages (stream 7)
[2026-04-02T13:01:06Z] decode: prefetch miss -> falling back to scalar-dequant path
[perf] prefill 8192 tokens batch=1: median per-token 4.6ms
[perf] decode first token (TTFT): 1180ms
[trace] fallback path costs +750ms
```

kevin: :eyes: fallback scalar-dequant path explains the TTFT spike. microbatching will create many small KV fragments and cause eviction/rehydration churn. what's your microbatch config?

sara: microbatch=8, microbatch_threshold=64. repro command I used: ```bash
rwinf bench --model redwood-m-hybrid-fp8 --seq 8192 --batch 1 --microbatch 8 --iters 20
```

nate: hypothesis: kernel-router prefers packed-gemm fp8 for throughput but that kernel expects contiguous KV pages; with microbatching we fragment KV and force a slow path that does dequant+copy. For long context decode we should bias router to decode-optimized kernels (lower cold-start latency) even if nominal TPS is lower.

dmitri: also check calibration: last week's calibration pass toggled per-layer int8 fallback for some attention layers — that could change codepath selection during decode. can we surface a "calibration flags" section in profiler?

sara: ran a quick config change: KV_PREFETCH=1 and microbatch=0 on the same workload. results: TTFT -> 420ms, TPS +1.7x. so KV fragmentation looks like the main culprit.

kevin: good data. propose a two-part mitigation: 1) tune kernel-router to prefer decode-optimized kernels when seq>4096 or request.has_long_prefill, 2) make microbatch threshold adaptive based on active KV fragmentation metric.

nate: implementation note — add a lightweight KV-frag counter in scheduler (increment on non-contiguous allocs) and expose as metric. router policy can consult it cheaply.

sara: i pushed a small canary patch to add router mode "prefill_aware" that biases decode kernel selection and skips aggressive packed fusion for long prefill. patch: ```diff
--- router/v2
+++ router/v2
@@ -112,6 +112,12 @@
+  if (request.seq_len > 4096 || metrics.kv_frag_score > 0.2) {
+    route.prefer_decode_latency = true
+  }
```

ci-bot: deploy canary 2026-04-02T14:12:00 - route 5% traffic -> nodepool-fp8-prefill-aware

kevin: canary results after 10k long-ctx requests: median TTFT 410ms (was 1180ms), 95p 780ms (was 2.1s). TPS on decode steady +30% for long sequences. tail still exists on pathological fragmentation.

dmitri: promising. we should also log calibration decisions during model load so we can correlate runtime fallsbacks to calibration flags.

sara: opening INF-3212 with repro, raw traces, and the canary numbers. will follow up to make microbatch_threshold adaptive and add calibration logs.

kevin: once INF-3212 has root cause and mitigations, schedule a perf-test gate to prevent the router change from regressing short-context TPS.

sara: agreed. next steps: ship adaptive microbatch threshold, add KV-frag metric, and calibration visibility. thanks all. :thumbsup:
